synopsis: GeoWAM places predicted geometry between camera observations and driving trajectories. A DVGT-2 encoder supplies historical geometry and ego tokens; a forecasting decoder predicts future geometric features, which condition a separate ego decoder through a detached connection. The planner consumes these latent features rather than reconstructed future images or point clouds directly. Reported geometry and NAVSIM results favor the complete system, but the paper does not isolate the contribution of forecasting through ablations. [e03, e04, e06, e07, e11, e12, e14, e16]

problem.text: The authors argue that future-image prediction entangles motion and spatial structure with appearance, so visual plausibility need not imply a representation suited to planning. They investigate whether forecasting metric geometry provides more useful supervision for driving policies. Geometry targets come from existing geometry models, avoiding the ground-truth occupancy annotations required by the occupancy-based approaches discussed in the paper.

contributions.text: Extends visual geometry reconstruction into forecasting: historical multiview images predict future geometric features and dense point maps under feature, point-regression, confidence and surface-normal supervision.

Introduces an inverse-dynamics-like action branch that infers future ego tokens from predicted geometry and historical memory, then directly regresses one trajectory. The geometry-to-ego connection blocks gradients from the trajectory objective through the predicted geometry tokens.

Reports improved aggregate geometry accuracy and the highest EPDMS among the methods listed for both NAVSIM evaluation splits. These comparisons establish performance of the complete recipe, rather than independently establishing which architectural component causes the gains.

inputs: Historical multiview RGB images I_{t-K+1:t}; the reported configuration uses three historical frames. [e03, e09]
Training-only supervision: future RGB images for detached feature targets, dense point-map targets and validity masks, ego trajectories, and historical relative poses. [e05, e07]
outputs: Future dense point maps and per-pixel confidence maps; each point map is expressed in its corresponding future ego coordinate frame. [e04]
One future ego trajectory containing planar position and heading, expressed in the current ego coordinate frame. [e07]

steps.name: Encode historical geometry and motion context
steps.detail: The DVGT-2 geometry encoder retains several feature levels. Each historical time and camera contributes spatial geometry tokens and ego tokens; concatenating these forms the historical memory Z_t. The forecasting and action branches both access this memory.

steps.name: Forecast future geometric features
steps.detail: A learned geometry-query seed is replicated across future times, camera views and spatial positions, with temporal, view and two-dimensional position embeddings. Decoder layers apply causal temporal self-attention and cross-attention to historical memory. Level-specific projections transform the resulting future latent U_hat into features for the shared geometry head, which outputs point maps and confidence.

steps.name: Infer future ego tokens
steps.detail: A separate decoder initializes learned ego queries for every future time, view and ego-token slot. After causal temporal self-attention, queries attend to historical memory and detached predicted geometry latents. This is the paper's inverse-dynamics-like step: predicted scene evolution conditions a learned ego-motion representation.

steps.name: Regress a trajectory
steps.detail: The action head concatenates deepest-level historical ego tokens with predicted future ego tokens and refines them using a causal temporal transformer. A learned trajectory query cross-attends to these features, and a regression head produces positions and headings. There are no trajectory anchors, mode classes or iterative action sampling.

training.text: Geometry pretraining combines OpenScene, nuScenes, Bench2Drive, Waymo Open Dataset, KITTI, Argoverse 2 and DDAD. It predicts eight future frames at 2 Hz from three historical frames, dynamically sampling two to eight views. The encoder and point head initialize from DVGT-2. Training runs for 161 epochs with AdamW, weight decay 0.05, bfloat16, 5% linear warmup and cosine decay. Peak learning rates are 0.0001 for the future decoder and 0.00002 for pretrained components; the future decoder has six layers, width 1024 and 16 attention heads.

Future images enter only a target branch using the same geometry encoder; their feature targets are detached. Current-frame point supervision anchors reconstruction alongside future prediction. Planning jointly finetunes the complete model on NAVSIM navtrain for 40 epochs using eight views and three historical frames. The future decoder and new action head use learning rate 0.0001; remaining pretrained parameters use 0.00002. Both trajectory and auxiliary historical-pose loss weights are 5.

inference.text: Inference uses historical images without future-image targets. Geometry features are forecast first, then consumed by the ego decoder and trajectory head. Although dense point maps are predicted outputs, the action branch conditions on future geometry latents, so the described information path does not require feeding decoded point clouds into the planner.

In navhard, feedback is supplied by the evaluation system: after a predicted trajectory determines a new ego pose, a 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction renders another observation for replanning. This is pseudo-closed-loop benchmark feedback; the paper does not report physical vehicle execution.

equations.expression: L_feat = (1/(F L)) Σ_k Σ_ell [1 − cos(X_hat_{t+k}^ell, sg(X_bar_{t+k}^ell))]; L_pre = L_feat + L_point^future + L_point^current.
equations.explanation: F counts future steps and L retained feature levels. Predicted features match detached future-image features through cosine distance averaged over cameras and patches. Each point-map objective combines Euclidean regression, confidence-aware regression and multiscale surface-normal consistency over valid pixels.

Equation (9) makes the information flow explicit: ego queries attend to observed history and forecast geometry. Stop-gradient preserves the forward conditioning signal while blocking its backward gradient path; it does not remove the decoder's separate access to historical memory.

equations.expression: L_plan = L_pre + λ_traj L_traj + λ_pose L_pose; λ_traj = λ_pose = 5.
equations.explanation: Planning retains geometry pretraining losses and adds L1 trajectory supervision plus an auxiliary L1 loss for relative poses between historical frames. The pose loss is a training objective, rather than a separately described inference-time control procedure.

results.setting: nuScenes validation; mean over all eight predicted frames spanning four seconds. Generated-video baselines are converted to geometry using DVGT.
results.metric: Mean ray-depth Abs Rel, lower is better; mean δ < 1.25, higher is better
results.interpretation: Reported geometric forecasting results favor GeoWAM under the common output metric. The video baseline measures the combined generator-and-reconstructor pipeline, so the comparison does not isolate representation choice under matched training resources. These values measure predicted geometry, not executed driving.
The aggregate improvement does not hold for every horizon and metric: the video-based pipeline has higher threshold accuracy at one second.

results.setting: NAVSIM v2 navtest with the official human-penalty protocol; Table 2 labels this closed-loop planning.
results.comparison: DVGT-2: 89.6, giving the reported improvement of 0.6 score points.
results.interpretation: GeoWAM has the highest aggregate score in the table. EPDMS combines compliance, safety, progress and comfort components; an aggregate win does not imply leadership on every component or demonstrate on-road deployment.

results.setting: NAVSIM v2 challenging scenarios; original scenes followed by synthetic reactive scenes under the pseudo-closed-loop protocol and official human penalties.
results.metric: Reported two-stage EPDMS, higher is better
results.comparison: EponaV2†: 36.1; DVGT-2: 31.7. The dagger identifies methods using reinforcement learning or PDMS-score supervision.
results.interpretation: GeoWAM has the highest reported score among the listed methods, including the specially supervised entries. Supervision differs across methods, and this benchmark score is neither a physical-driving success percentage nor a directly interchangeable measure with navtest EPDMS.

limitations.text: The supplied experiments contain no mechanism ablation or uncertainty estimates. They do not isolate geometry pretraining, future-token conditioning, stop-gradient, or additional training from one another. Consequently, the performance differences support the complete system more strongly than the proposed causal explanation.

Geometry evaluation reduces each predicted point to its distance from the ego origin. These ray-depth metrics do not directly establish full three-dimensional correspondence accuracy or the separation of ego motion from surrounding-agent motion.

Detaching future geometry blocks one trajectory-gradient path, but the ego decoder also reads shared historical memory and the full model is jointly finetuned. The architecture therefore does not by itself guarantee that action supervision cannot change the geometry encoder through another path.

The forecasting equations contain no candidate-action input, and the action head predicts one trajectory. The supplied method does not establish counterfactual evaluation of alternative actions or explicit handling of multiple plausible future trajectories.

The authors interpret qualitative examples as evidence of coherent structures, surrounding-vehicle dynamics and obstacle avoidance. Only their descriptions and captions were supplied here, so those visual claims were not independently inspected; the quantitative evaluations remain geometry metrics and simulation-based planning scores.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires the DVGT-2 initialization, the seven-dataset pretraining mixture, geometry target generation, supervised trajectories and historical poses, and NAVSIM evaluation assets. The text supplies major optimization settings but leaves dataset sizes and mixture weights, split-level accounting, image resolution, batch size, hardware and runtime unspecified. The precise dense-target generation, validity masking and point-loss implementation also need clarification. In particular, nuScenes pretraining partitions must be checked against the validation evaluation split.

A focused mechanism test would hold initialization, data and training budget fixed while retraining with and without future-geometry attention in the ego decoder. A separate comparison would enable versus block gradients through that connection. Reporting both geometry metrics and NAVSIM scores across seeds would test whether forecasting information improves planning and whether detachment preserves geometry. These are proposed experiments, not results reported or reproduced here.

reasoning.text: The recorded Q4 classification is supported at the module level: a pretrained geometry forecaster feeds a distinct ego decoder and trajectory head through a one-way detached connection. This architectural separation supports Dual-system despite a shared encoder and joint finetuning. IDM should retain the authors' inverse-dynamics-like qualification: ego motion is inferred from forecast geometry and history, rather than obtained from a conventional inverse model over measured state transitions. The multiview, geometric and driving subcategories follow directly from the inputs, prediction targets and evaluations.

discussionQuestions: With initialization, data and compute matched, how much planning improvement comes specifically from attending to predicted future geometry? [e06, e09, e16]
Does the detached connection preserve forecasting when action gradients can still update shared historical representations? [e03, e06, e07]
Which geometric errors best predict recovery failures under navhard's rendered feedback, beyond aggregate ray-depth accuracy? [e10, e13]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author block, date, arXiv stamp and project link
evidence.detail: The title, identifier and author list match the catalog. The stamp identifies version 2608.23486v2 and 25 August 2026; the title-page date is 26 August 2026. A project URL is listed.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–3, Section 1, motivation and contribution list
evidence.detail: The authors motivate geometry forecasting as supervision aligned with spatial motion and planning, arguing that pixel prediction entangles physical structure with appearance.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Section 3.1, Multiview geometry encoding, Eq. (1)
evidence.detail: DVGT-2 encodes historical multiview images into multilevel geometry and ego tokens, concatenated into historical memory Z_t.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Future geometry decoding, Eqs. (2)–(4)
evidence.detail: Learned future queries use temporal and view embeddings plus spatial positional embeddings. Temporal self-attention and history cross-attention produce future latents; projected features decode to point maps and confidence in each future ego frame.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Future geometry supervision, Eqs. (5)–(7)
evidence.detail: Future-image features from the same encoder are detached targets. Pretraining combines cosine feature alignment with future and current point objectives comprising regression, confidence-aware regression and surface-normal consistency.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Future ego-token decoding, Eqs. (8)–(9)
evidence.detail: Ego queries undergo causal temporal attention and attend to both historical memory and detached future geometry. The authors describe this geometry-conditioned motion inference as inverse-dynamics-like.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Trajectory decoding and Planning objective, Eqs. (10)–(11)
evidence.detail: Historical and predicted ego tokens feed a temporal transformer and trajectory query. A head directly regresses one current-frame planar trajectory. Finetuning retains geometry losses and adds L1 trajectory and historical relative-pose losses.

GeoWAM uses dense metric point-map targets derived from off-the-shelf geometry foundation models instead of ground-truth occupancy annotations; the geometry learning comparison is described as requiring RGB images.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Datasets and Implementation details
evidence.detail: Lists seven pretraining datasets, nuScenes validation, NAVSIM splits, three history frames, eight future frames at 2 Hz, view counts, decoder dimensions, 161 pretraining epochs, 40 planning epochs, learning rates, optimizer settings and loss weights.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Metrics; Section 4.2, baseline protocol
evidence.detail: Point maps become ego-origin ray depths evaluated by Abs Rel and threshold accuracy. EPDMS combines nine driving components under human penalties. Epona and Cosmos predictions undergo DVGT reconstruction before geometry evaluation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, GeoWAM, Epona + DVGT and VGGT-World rows; mean columns and one-second threshold column
evidence.detail: Mean Abs Rel/threshold accuracy are 0.257/0.754 for GeoWAM, 0.274/0.655 for Epona + DVGT and 0.325/0.544 for VGGT-World. One-second threshold accuracy is 0.708 for GeoWAM and 0.732 for Epona + DVGT.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Table 2, EPDMS column, GeoWAM and DVGT-2 rows; Section 4.3.1
evidence.detail: GeoWAM scores 90.2 EPDMS against DVGT-2's 89.6. The accompanying text identifies the 0.6-point improvement and highest overall score in the table.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Datasets; PDF p. 8, Section 4.3.2
evidence.detail: Navhard evaluates original and synthetic reactive scenes. A 3DGS-based benchmark renders observations from trajectory-induced ego poses and feeds them back for subsequent planning; the text reports GeoWAM EPDMS of 36.6.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 3, EPDMS column and caption
evidence.detail: The leaderboard reports GeoWAM at 36.6, EponaV2† at 36.1 and DVGT-2 at 31.7. Dagger-marked methods use reinforcement learning or PDMS-score supervision.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.4; PDF p. 9, Figure 3 caption
evidence.detail: The text describes aggregated future geometry and ego poses for left turns, straight driving and right turns, with qualitative claims about structure, another vehicle's motion and roadside-vehicle avoidance.

The supplied evaluation contains geometry comparisons, NAVSIM planning comparisons and qualitative discussion. It provides no mechanism ablation, seed variability, confidence intervals or physical vehicle execution results.

The method and implementation text specify objectives and major training settings but omit a complete target-generation and masking recipe, dataset mixture accounting, batch size, image resolution and hardware/runtime information.
